Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Teacher R was new this year. He tried to impose his own teaching and grading methods, which were very different from what we've experienced before. Even if his methods were wrong, we were still expected to follow them. He took points off for scratch work he didn't like and tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this. He also took forever to grade our assignments. We took a test the week before spring break and got it back about six weeks later. He refused to go over it with anyone. He never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. The administration noticed these issues, and we were informed that R wasn't coming back next year. We were all overjoyed about this. Since the announcement, R completely checked out. He just wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. Yesterday, as I was walking out of R's classroom for the last time, I called over my shoulder, "See you next year!" My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. Is AITA (Ask If Truly Asshole)? Alright, so I need to determine if my action was right or wrong. Let's break it down. First, I should consider the context. Teacher R was not performing well, was unfair in grading, and was generally unpleasant. The administration decided he wasn't coming back, and the students were happy about this. R, after the announcement, stopped putting effort into his teaching, went to Disneyland, and didn't engage with the students. I said "See you next year!" as I was leaving the classroom for the last time. My friends think I'm being an asshole, but I don't see it that way. So, why might my friends think I'm the asshole? Maybe they think it's mean or disrespectful to say that to someone who's being let go. They might feel that it's not kind to remind him that he's not coming back, especially since he's already checked out. On the other hand, I might see it as a harmless comment. I was just saying goodbye, and since he's not coming back, I thought it was a way to acknowledge that. I didn't mean any harm, just a casual farewell. But perhaps there's more to it. Maybe the way I said it came off as mocking or sarcastic. If I said it with a certain tone or expression, it could be interpreted differently. Or maybe it's just the content of the message itself that's problematic. I should also consider how Teacher R might have felt upon hearing that. He was already checked out, barely talking, and not engaging. Maybe hearing that from a student who was happy about his departure could have been hurtful or irritating. Alternatively, maybe it's not about the message itself but the timing. Saying it as I was leaving for the last time might have been seen as taking advantage of the situation or rubbing it in that he's not coming back. I also need to think about the broader implications. Is it appropriate for a student to make comments about a teacher's employment status? Should I be more considerate of the teacher's feelings, even if I don't agree with his methods or attitude? Perhaps my friends are concerned that by making such a comment, I'm being disrespectful or unprofessional, even if I didn't intend it that way. They might think that it's better to keep such thoughts to myself, especially in a public setting like a classroom. Moreover, considering that Teacher R was already disengaged and hostile, maybe my comment could have been seen as adding to the negativity, even if I didn't mean it that way. On the flip side, I might argue that it was just a simple farewell and that I didn't mean any harm. I was just acknowledging the situation, and since he wasn't coming back, it was a way to say goodbye without any negative intent. But I can see how others might interpret it differently.
